statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band and well below the block threshold because the observed NQ overnight path is a two-sided 87.75-point range that retraced roughly 37 points off a fresh low, while Stress sits in the elevated band on a 4.78% 10-year Treasury yield, WTI above $86 and an open September Federal Reserve rate-hike debate.
recommendation: Conditions are described as ordinary in price-path terms and materially stressed in macro terms. A narrow evidence-based caution window is mapped from 13:30 to 16:00 UTC, covering the US cash open, the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS pair and the first hour of repricing, where the forecast policy state steps to WATCH for two clock-hours before returning to EA_ON.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a two-sided overnight range while a 4.78% 10-year yield, the highest since January 2025, and firmer crude carry the macro stress
body: NQ futures trade at 29,472.25, down 0.14%, inside a Globex range of 29,434.75-29,522.50. A fresh overnight low printed in the past hour and was followed by a retracement of about 37 points, so the path shows no directional efficiency, no repeated extension after failed pullbacks and no holding near the session extreme. ES futures are effectively flat at 7,697.00, down 0.03%. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 31 August at 29,456.97, up 0.08% within a 29,304.49-29,483.90 range, and VIX ended at 14.92. The macro backdrop is considerably more stressed than the price path. The US 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to about 4.78%, its highest level since January 2025, extending the bear steepening that began after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh used Jackson Hole to warn that inflation has not meaningfully slowed; CME FedWatch pricing for a hike at the 15-16 September meeting has been running in the 60-66% area. Energy is the second stress channel: US forces destroyed Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island as Tehran prepared to fire mine-carrying rockets into the Strait of Hormuz, Iran responded against US positions in Jordan, and threats have been extended to the Kharg Island export hub. WTI trades at $86.64, up 1.03%, and Brent at $88.98, up 0.69%, while gold is marginally higher at $4,489.40. The decisive point for this assessment is that equity futures are not confirming the yield and crude moves; that cross-asset conflict raises Stress and reduces directional conviction rather than establishing the persistent one-way structure that Tail measures. The shared Finviz cross-asset context file was approximately 156 minutes old at assessment time and therefore outside its 90-minute freshness bound, so it was not used as supporting evidence and this assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research. Risk concentrates on the scheduled 13:05 to 14:30 UTC block rather than on current conditions.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed between 5 and 17 across 31 August and into the overnight session, with the policy state mapped to EA_ON in every hour. Stress rose from the high-30s in the Asian session to the low-to-mid 50s once the Gulf escalation, the crude advance and the long-end yield rise were absorbed through European and US hours, and has since held near 50-53. Dominant mode was mixed apart from an event/whipsaw phase around 09:00-10:00 UTC, and confidence ranged from 84 to 88.
outlookSummary: The base case is a continuation of ordinary, two-sided conditions through the remaining Asian and European hours, with conditional Tail easing to 9 in the quietest windows. Risk concentrates on the 13:00-16:00 UTC block covering the Fed Barr remarks, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS pair, where forecast Tail peaks at 22 and the mapped policy state steps to WATCH for two clock-hours before decaying back into the low band through the US afternoon. A secondary checkpoint sits at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress stays in the low-fifties to low-sixties across the whole horizon because crude, the long end of the Treasury curve and the September rate-hike question are all unresolved into ADP, ISM Services and August payrolls later this week.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NQ 29,472.25 (-0.14%) inside an 87.75-point Globex range of 29,434.75-29,522.50, having printed a fresh overnight low and then retraced about 37 points. The retracement is genuine, so structure stays two-sided and Tail holds in the low band while a 4.78% 10-year and $86.64 WTI carry the stress.
drivers: NQ two-sided in 29,434.75-29,522.50; ~37-point bounce off the overnight low
US 10-year at ~4.78%, highest since January 2025, on September hike pricing
WTI $86.64 (+1.03%) and Brent $88.98 on the renewed US-Iran flare-up
